end.note: Ends at the LHC-wide start of Long Shutdown 3 (June 2026); mirrors experiment:totem.
CERN schedule: the LHC resumes operation in mid-2030; the rest of the CERN complex restarts in stages from mid-2028.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: The detector record carries the same Long Shutdown 3 interval as experiment:totem, whose interval note gives the evidence and CERN's wording for the bounds; the state is inferred from the LHC being shut down.
intervals.quote: Following its final physics run, the accelerator has been switched off to begin CERN’s Long Shutdown 3 (LS3) ... The HiLumi LHC, scheduled to begin operation in 2030

placements.note: TOTEM's Roman Pots and T1/T2 telescopes extend along the beamline well beyond the CMS cavern itself, but share the same interaction point; the detector is placed at the existing site:cern-point-5-cms.
placements.quote: As CERN’s ‘longest’ experiment, TOTEM detectors are spread across almost half a kilometre around the CMS interaction point.

total_mass.quote: TOTEM has almost 3,000 kg of equipment

summary.plain: TOTEM's detectors: 26 Roman Pots that creep to within a millimetre of the LHC beam to catch protons scattered at tiny angles, plus two tracking telescopes covering the forward direction around the CMS collision point.
summary.technical: Roman Pot silicon-strip stations (26 total) symmetric about IP5, plus T1 (CSC) and T2 (GEM) forward tracking telescopes covering pseudo-rapidity 3-7; ~3000 kg total equipment.

technology.quote: Two particle tracking telescopes (T1 and T2) using cathode-strip chambers and Gas Electron Multipliers (GEM) to track collision products; twenty-six Roman Pot detectors equipped with silicon sensors to measure scattered protons.
technology.value: Roman Pot silicon-strip detectors plus T1 (cathode strip chamber) and T2 (Gas Electron Multiplier) forward tracking telescopes
